body.rationale: The governing IPS is a draft, so I weight IPS compliance with some caution. Even so, a CIO needs portfolios that can be built from and that sit near the policy band. My first choice is pc_researcher. It is the best blend of covariance-aware construction and diversification: 7.2 effective assets, 0.51 Sharpe, 10.9% backtest drawdown, a CRO risk of 0.33, and only two soft-ish breaches (volatility and tracking error) rather than structural ones. Reviewers did flag that its delivered portfolio does not match the near-1/N narrative and that the Sharpe sits above the stated floor. Those are fixable disclosure issues, not a flawed portfolio. Second is resampled_efficient_frontier. It has no IPS breaches, 13.3 effective assets, and a clean intra-category review that found no execution error. The one technical error, the description of gamma, is a wording problem. Its main risk is thin drawdown headroom (-24.3% vs -25%). Third is black_litterman. It also has no breaches, 6.1 effective assets, and a reviewer who recomputed its numbers and found them consistent. The one technical error, the claim about Omega shrinkage, is a mechanism misdescription. Fourth is cvar_minimization. It has no breaches, a non-Gaussian tail objective that complements the covariance-based names, and the lowest drawdown among the compliant return-optimised group (-18.7%). Its tuning to the volatility edge and its reliance on a few crisis episodes are real weaknesses. Fifth is max_sharpe. It is IPS-compliant and has the strongest ex-ante Sharpe among the compliant names. It concentrates 46% in us_value, which both its reviewers flagged, so it ranks last of the five. My first choice beats my fifth because pc_researcher gets a similar or better Sharpe with much more diversification and a drawdown less than half as deep (-10.9% vs -24.7%), and without depending on a single value-vs-growth CMA gap. I rank the compliant return-optimised names above the other risk-structured and heuristic ones. My own family (risk_structured) is excluded from my vote except for maximum_diversification and HRP, which I left out: they are 82-92% cash and breach all three hard limits. The bottom flag is market_cap_weight. It has the worst drawdown (-40.6%) and the highest CRO risk (0.80), and it breaches the drawdown limit. Reviewers also showed that its ETF-AUM proxy is not a valid capitalisation weight (double-counted overlapping equity styles, meaningless gold and commodity sizes). The CIO should not lean on it.
